title: Bijli Sooraj Se 5 Guna Garam!
idea: A lightning bolt heats the air to about 27,700°C, roughly 5 times hotter than the Sun's surface. The record bolt was 829 km long, and counting the seconds before the thunder tells you how far away it struck.

lines.text: Ek bijli Sooraj ki surface se paanch guna zyada garam hoti hai!
Sooraj ki surface lagbhag 5,500 degree, aur bijli? Lagbhag 27,700 degree Celsius!
Record todne wali bijli 829 km lambi thi, Mumbai se Bengaluru jitni!
Yeh Mount Everest se 90 guna lambi, yaani lagbhag 1000 Burj Khalifa!
Roshni turant pahunchti hai, par aawaz ko har km mein 3 second lagte.
Toh garaj tak seconds gino, 3 se divide karo, kitne km door? Try karoge?

facts.claim: Lightning heats the air it passes through to about 50,000°F (about 27,700°C), which is 5 times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
The Sun's visible surface (photosphere) is about 10,000°F, or 5,500°C.
WMO certified a world-record 829 km (515 miles) megaflash on 22 October 2017, running from eastern Texas to near Kansas City. Mumbai to Bengaluru is about 840 km in a straight line.
829 km is about 94 times Mount Everest's height (8.849 km) and about 1,000 times the Burj Khalifa's height (828 m).

Sound travels at about 343 m/s (about 1,235 km/h), so it takes about 3 seconds per km. Light travels at about 1.08 billion km/h, so it arrives almost instantly. The flash-to-bang count divided by 3 gives the distance in km.
